lancelot.summary: Jungle assassin built on the sequence of dashes, with a window of invulnerability during the ultimate.
lancelot.analysis:
Lancelot goes through a fight rather than entering it. Its skill 1 marks the first unmarked enemy it passes through, and each new mark resets its recharge: well chained, it can dash almost without interruption as long as it finds a target to mark. His skill 2 makes him untouchable during his three strikes.

His ultimate makes him invulnerable during the animation, which also makes it a defensive tool to dodge a check or an execution. The hero is punished by anything that blocks movement – ​​Khufra in the lead – and by areas that prevent him from moving forward.

gusion.summary: Combo Magic Assassin: He throws his daggers, slips behind the marked target, and recalls them to inflict all his damage at once.
gusion.analysis:
Gusion is the most demanding combo hero in the game after Fanny. All of his skills can be rerolled, and the order and timing of the rerolls entirely determine his damage. The standard combo is to put the daggers down, get close with the ultimate, then trigger the recovery so everything happens simultaneously.

A mastered Gusion takes out any fragile target in less than a second, often before the opponent's screen has shown anything. A rough Gusion does a third of the damage and dies on the spot. Few heroes have such a wide gap between the two.

ling.summary: Assassin who moves on walls, out of range, and chooses his moment to fall on a target.
ling.analysis:
Ling changes the geometry of the map. While on a wall, he is untouchable by most ground skills, allowing him to wait indefinitely for the opening. It does not use mana but an energy resource, which limits the number of consecutive jumps.

His ultimate makes him invulnerable while jumping, then slows and knocks enemies into the air upon landing. The hero is excellent in mobile skirmishing and weak against a grouped team that keeps his controls to himself. Khufra remains his clearest response.

yi-sun-shin.summary: Hybrid jungler who switches from bow to sword depending on the distance, and whose ultimate reveals the entire map.
yi-sun-shin.analysis:
Yi Sun-shin changes weapons on his own: he shoots a bow from afar and strikes with a sword on contact, and each change strengthens his next two attacks. His skill 1 propels him forward by briefly rendering him immune to controls, and his recharge decreases with each successful weapon change. The ultimate first gives him vision of the entire map and an acceleration, then, restarted, sends a ship which stuns the center of the zone before a barrage which slows down: it is as much an information tool as a remote initiation.

His measured performance is concentrated at the start of the game: his victory rate is significantly higher in games finished before the twelfth minute, then returns to around the average. He therefore lives from the advance gained in the jungle rather than from the end of the game, and his only protection against controls only lasts an instant. The measurements place him in difficulty against Karina, Uranus, Aamon, Johnson and Hayabusa, from Mythic rank to Mythic Glory rank.

selena.summary: Heroine with two forms: traps and stun arrow from a distance, then assassination on contact after the ultimate.
selena.analysis:
Selena is played in two stages. In her elven form, she places demons that watch over a location and cling to passing enemies, and she shoots an arrow whose stun lengthens with the distance traveled; his skills leave marks on targets. The ultimate switches her to Abyssal Form, where her skills become a leaping attack with shield and a charge, which consume these marks for additional damage; she can then return to elven form.

This versatility has a cost: its entire initiation relies on the arrow, which must start from afar to stun for a long time. His measured win rate remains below average at all ranks, with a low point in games lasting less than twelve minutes. It is played in Mid lane as well as in roam, with different objects depending on the position. The measurements place her in difficulty against Gloo, Popol and Kupa, Chip and Lolita.

aamon.summary: Magic assassin camouflaged by every skill that hits; his ultimate finishes all the better if the target is injured.
aamon.analysis:
Aamon alternates camouflage and reinforced attacks. Each skill that hits an enemy camouflages him: he can no longer be targeted, recovers HP and gains speed; upon exiting this state, his basic attacks for the next few seconds are strengthened, deal magic damage and reduce his cooldowns. His empowered attacks charge shards. The ultimate launches them all at a target: the more shards he has in reserve and on the ground, the longer the salvo is, and its damage increases as the target loses its HP.

His measured numbers are slightly below average at all ranks, with no big difference depending on game length; however, his pick rate has increased over the last thirty days. The measurements place him in difficulty against Gloo, Lolita, Silvanna, Hayabusa and Masha, and at ease against Cici, Marcel, Claude and Bruno.

nolan.summary: Jungle assassin who cuts rifts with each skill: two rifts that touch attract enemies, explode and restore HP.
nolan.analysis:
Nolan plays on his flaws. Each skill leaves one, which slows down enemies; When two rifts touch, they pull enemies towards their center then explode, and each hero or monster hit restores energy and HP. His first two skills have very short recharges, one hits an area in front of him, the other makes him charge, and they chain together to make the faults cross. The ultimate slash an area three times, leaves three rifts there and triggers them as he retreats. After a few seconds without inflicting or receiving damage, his next basic attack causes him to leap onto the target, opening a rift.

He is hotly contested: fifth selection rate of all heroes, and a ban which has almost doubled over the last thirty days and climbs with the rank. His measured win rate remains around average, above in games lasting less than twelve minutes then below after the fourteenth minute. The measurements place him clearly in difficulty against Saber and Natalia, then against Jawhead and Hayabusa.

saber.summary: Single Target Assassin: his ultimate lifts an enemy hero and hits them three times, with Resilience making no difference.
saber.analysis:
Saber is built to take down a specific hero. His damage reduces the target's physical armor, stacking. His skill 1 spins five swords around him; during their duration, each sword strike hits its target and reduces his two cooldowns. His skill 2 makes him dash then strengthens his next basic attack, which launches him at the target and greatly slows it down. The ultimate makes him charge an enemy hero, knocks them airborne for a little over a second without Resilience reducing the effect, and strikes them three times.

His measured numbers change markedly with rank: below average win rate in Epic, above average in Mythic Glory, and highest bans in Legend and Mythic. He is especially strong in short games, above fifty-five percent before the fourteenth minute. In roam, his most played builds have a victory rate measured below average; his best measured partners are Diggie and Marcel. The measurements place him in difficulty against Balmond, Leomord, Baxia, Miya and Sun.

chou.summary: Isolation fighter: he extracts a target from the opposing group and kills it before his team reacts.
chou.analysis:
Chou is the roam hero with the highest mastery cap. The idea is simple – the ultimate repels a target and pursues it – but its execution relies on animation cancellations that the game nowhere explains. The reference combo chains skill 1, canceled jump, ultimate, then skill 2 to hold the target upon landing.

His interest in an organized team comes from there: he chooses who dies. Against a player who keeps his Purify, on the other hand, the ultimate loses half of its value, and Chou becomes an average fighter again.

His passive places stacks of Sha Residue on the heroes he hits; at five, they burst, healing him with each stack consumed and accelerating him, which makes him excellent as soon as there are several targets in range - a confrontation with five gives him much more return than a duel.

His ultimate makes him immune to checks while he advances, which also makes him a credible initiator. Countering it almost always involves reducing healing: without it, a well-equipped Yu Zhong absorbs an entire team.

paquito.summary: Window Fighter: Every three skills, the next one is improved, for a very short damage peak.
paquito.analysis:
Paquito is not played skill by skill but by sequences. Every three skills launched, he switches to Field Stance and obtains an improved version of a skill, even on recharge: his whole point lies in choosing the right one and placing it at the right time.

Well done, it takes out a weak target in two seconds from a considerable distance. Played poorly, he wastes his upgraded versions on minions and has nothing left. He is a rhythm hero, very sensitive to the player's level.

dyrroth.summary: Rage fighter who removes his target's physical armor before striking them, played in EXP lane and jungle.
dyrroth.analysis:
Dyrroth builds up rage while fighting; At mid-gauge, his first two skills become a reinforced version, with more range or more damage. Every two basic attacks he hits in a circle around himself and heals himself, and each hero hit shortens his cooldowns. Skill 2 launches it at a target then, recast, removes a large part of its physical armor for a few seconds: it is the opening which makes the rest of its damage effective. The ultimate leaves after a short delay, cannot be interrupted, and slows down everything it passes through.

He lives on his early game rallies: his measured win rate is highest in short games and drops below average after the eighteenth minute. Its numbers also vary depending on the rank, lower in Mythic than in Mythic Glory. The measures place him in difficulty against Masha, Benedetta and Thamuz.

sun.summary: Fighter who multiplies: his doubles strike with him, heal him and eat away at the targets' armor.
sun.analysis:
Sun fights by summoning doubles. His first two skills throw his staff, which leaves a temporary duplicate; the second additionally hides him while he moves with the stick. The ultimate summons a more durable duplicate, closer to its own stats. Each hit from Sun or his doubles reduces the target's physical armor a little, and each hit from a double heals it: the more doubles there are on a target, the faster it melts and the longer it lasts.

His measured profile is that of a late-game hero: below-average victory rate in games lasting less than fourteen minutes, then significantly above after the sixteenth. He is also very often banned, especially at Mythical rank. Double the ultimate takes increased damage, and the metrics put Sun in trouble against Aldous, Natan, Alucard, Joy, and Ruby.

guinevere.summary: Magic damage fighter who knocks her targets into the air, then holds them there under her ultimate.
guinevere.analysis:
Guinevere is built around projection. Her skill 2 makes her leap across an area, sending enemies into the air, then can launch herself again for a short teleport that leaves an illusion behind. She inflicts additional damage on targets in the air, and her hits mark enemies: a target with three marks is projected by her ultimate, which launches enemies already there into the air with each hit, while Guinevere remains unaffected by controls.

Everything therefore depends on skill 2: if the jump fails and the marks are missing, the ultimate loses most of its control. His measured numbers are close to average, a little better in short games, and his ban rate has fallen over the last thirty days. The measurements place her in difficulty against Masha, Wanwan, Khufra, Diggie and Fanny.

masha.summary: Fighter with three HP bars: each broken bar frees her from controls, and her basic attacks become area-of-effect claw strikes that heal her.
masha.analysis:
Masha plays on her three HP bars. Each one regains half of the HP provided by her items, and each bar that falls removes her control effects, blocks an attack and resets the recharge of Claw Strike. Skills that hit a hero open a wound on one side of the target; breaking this wound with a basic attack causes Masha to go wild, with resilience, attack speed, and movement speed, and changes her next three attacks to fan claw slashes that deal damage based on HP and heal her. The ultimate makes her charge an opposing hero, stunning them and pushing back enemies around them.

Her measured numbers are the highest in the game: leading win rate for all heroes at all ranks, above fifty-six percent regardless of game length, and a ban that climbs with rank, rare in Epic, in two out of three games in Mythic Glory. Patch 2.2.23 moved the slow from skill 1 to skill 2 and reduced the damage and healing of her claw strikes; her win rate has fallen slightly over the last thirty days. The measurements place her in difficulty against Freya, Estes, Bruno, Melissa and Floryn.

argus.summary: Critical fighter whose ultimate makes him unkillable for a few seconds, then heals him of all damage inflicted on heroes.
argus.analysis:
Argus relies on the critical hit: his passive immediately gives him a critical chance, and each critical becomes a demonic slash that ignores part of the armor and heals him. His skill 1 launches a hand that stuns the first enemy hit and brings them closer to each other, then launches into a rush followed by a large blow; his skill 2 counts as a basic attack, briefly stunning the hit hero and giving him attack speed. The ultimate removes his control effects and makes him immortal for a few seconds, then restores HP equal to the damage inflicted on heroes during this time. As long as it is off cooldown, it triggers on its own against a fatal blow.

He is one of the most effective heroes by metrics and one of the least banned: third highest win rate of all heroes, above fifty-five percent at each rank, for a ban of about one game in a hundred. His performance climbs with the duration of the game, just above average before the twelfth minute and beyond sixty percent from the sixteenth. The measurements place him in difficulty against Barats, Terizla, Uranus, Ruby and Fredrinn.

lukas.summary: Fighter who transforms into a sacred beast once his resolution gauge is full; his skill 1 changes depending on the attacks made before.
lukas.analysis:
Lukas fills his Resolve over time and, more quickly, by hurting heroes. Full, it allows him to transform into a sacred beast with his ultimate: all his attributes increase, his skills gain new effects, and a relaunch fires a shock wave; the form lasts as long as there is resolution. In both forms, everything goes through the sequence: his skill 2 makes him jump and reinforces his next attack, which puts him behind the target and speeds him up; each basic attack charges his skill 1, which briefly stuns and, at two charges, makes him immune to crowd control while he spins.

His measured figures are close to average, with a clear profile depending on duration: very low in games lasting less than twelve minutes, above average from the fourteenth. His ban rate, which increases with rank, has fallen significantly over the last thirty days. Patch 2.2.23 gave him more base HP and armor and shifted his skill 1 damage to his base rather than physical attack, to make defensive builds more viable. The measurements place him in difficulty against Phoveus, Balmond, Baxia, Valentina and Minsitthar.

freya.summary: Basic attack fighter, who charges orbs by hitting and spends them on attack speed, HP and dashes without base recharge.
freya.analysis:
Freya revolves around a resource: each basic attack gives her a holy orb, and each orb spent makes her next attack much faster and heals her. Her skill 2 has no base cooldown but costs two orbs: it is a rush that hurts and slows down, to alternate with basic attacks to keep the reserve full. Her skill 1 makes her jump over an area giving her a shield and throwing enemies into the air. The ultimate is a crowd-control-immune dive that slows enemies hit, then enters her Valkyrie state: her basic attacks then deal area damage.

Her measured numbers depend on rank and duration: below-average win rate from Epic to Mythic Honor, above average in Mythic Glory, and significantly better in games lasting less than twelve minutes than beyond the fourteenth. Patch 2.2.23 restored HP for each orb spent and lengthened the cooldown of her ultimate. Her ban rate has almost doubled over the last thirty days. The measures place her in difficulty against Minsitthar, Phoveus, Baxia, Edith and Franco.

aulus.summary: Simple fighter to learn: each skill that hits strengthens his basic attacks, and his ultimate strikes repeatedly around him.
aulus.analysis:
Aulus fights in waves of ax strikes. Each skill that deals damage gives him a few seconds of boosted basic attacks: they hit in a line, heal him, slightly slow enemies, and extend his range a bit. His skill 1 removes his slows and speeds him up; if he is not crowd-controlled within two seconds, he becomes immune to crowd control. His skill 2 strikes in a fan and stuns briefly, then springs back into a leap. The ultimate hits four times around him then a large final hit, reducing the damage he takes.

His measured numbers are above average, especially in short games: his win rate is highest before the twelfth minute and drops back to average after the twentieth. His ban rate, which increases with rank, has fallen sharply over the last thirty days. Patch 2.2.16a weakened his empowered attacks and lengthened the cooldown of his skill 1, while increasing the base damage of his ultimate. The measurements place him in difficulty against Alice, Floryn, Estes, Yve and Zhuxin.

alucard.summary: Jungle fighter who pounces on his target after each skill, and whose ultimate grants him permanent lifesteal and splits his recharges.
alucard.analysis:
Alucard alternates skills and basic attacks: after each skill, his next attack makes him jump on the target. His skill 1 makes him jump over an area, slowing down enemies, his skill 2 hits everything around him. His ultimate permanently gives him hybrid lifesteal; when cast, it slows enemies in the area and reduces their resistances, raises his own for each hero hit and halves the cooldown of his other skills for a few seconds, before a relaunch which sends a shock wave forward.

He is one of the least banned heroes, with numbers measuring slightly below average at all ranks. He is weak in short games and only exceeds the average from the fourteenth minute, without much difference thereafter. The measurements place him in difficulty against Fredrinn, Phoveus, Khufra, Barats and Thamuz, and comfortable against Natalia, Sun, Mathilda and Saber.

aldous.summary: Fighter who accumulates permanent charges by finishing off units, and whose ultimate reveals all enemy heroes before sending him at one of them.
aldous.analysis:
Aldous is built over time. His skill 1 strengthens his next basic attack, and each completed unit or hero hit with this attack gives him permanent charges that increase his damage, up to a thousand; he also gains some when his allies finish off units near him. His skill 2 puts him in a defensive posture, with a reduction in damage taken, then deals damage around him and stuns them, the longer the posture lasted. The ultimate gives him the vision of all the enemy heroes for a few seconds, then makes him rush towards one of them to push him back, interrupting a possible return to base.

No hero has such a marked gap depending on the length of the game: very low in games lasting less than twelve minutes, his measured win rate approaches sixty percent from the eighteenth. All ranks combined, he is above average and up over thirty days, for almost zero bans. Patch 2.2.23 shortened the cooldown of his skill 2 and increased his damage reduction in the late game. The measures place him in difficulty against Esmeralda, Karina, Cyclops, Estes and Popol and Kupa.

badang.summary: Obstacle fighter: he creates a wall behind his target and throws him there to stun him, and can be played both in roam and in EXP lane.
badang.analysis:
Badang plays with obstacles. After four basic attacks, the next one pushes back, and the breaths from his skills push back directly: an enemy thrown against an obstacle is stunned. His skill 2 makes him rush while gaining a shield; if he hits a hero, he stops and creates an obstacle right behind them. His skill 1, on two charges, sends a breath that hurts, slows down and pushes back, enough to pin the target against this wall. The ultimate chains a flurry of punches in one direction making him immune to crowd control.

His measured numbers are average at all ranks, with a slight edge in short games, and he gets picked quite often. Played in roam as well as in EXP lane, he mostly builds defense items: HP, armor and resistances rather than damage. The measurements place him in difficulty against Karina, Lolita, Esmeralda, Khufra and Phoveus, and at ease against Fanny, Sun and Zilong.

alpha.analysis:

The ultimate sends Beta to stun an area, then Alpha jumps there, knocking enemies in his path airborne to carry them to the point of impact.

His measured numbers are a little below average, with no notable difference depending on the length of the game. He is mostly played at lower ranks: his pick rate drops with each rank from Epic to Mythic Glory, and he is very rarely banned. Patch 2.2.16 strengthened the healing of his skill 2. The measures place him in difficulty against Benedetta, X.Borg, Valir, Lylia and Wanwan.

Kagura has eight skills in practice for three hits. Each spell has a version with an umbrella and a version without, and knowing what state you are in is the hero's main thing. The signature combo is the sending of the umbrella, its recovery which stuns around it, then the ultimate to push back.

She is also one of the rare mages capable of getting out of a bad position on her own, since her skill 2 frees her from all its negative effects by making her jump. In return, a status error leaves her without mobility in the middle of the opposing team.

pharsa.summary: Artillery Mage: His ultimate strikes across the map, without ever entering combat.

Pharsa plays on the scope. Her ultimate is a channeled bombardment covering a huge area at long range, allowing her to participate in a fight she barely sees. Well placed, this spell alone can decide a confrontation around the Lord.

His skill 1 marks the enemies hit, which his next attack or skill stuns; his skill 2, an online shock, does most of his damage between two ultimates. It has no movement of its own. The weak point is obvious: during the ultimate she is immobile and defenseless, and any assassin who finds her kills her.

cecilion.analysis:
Cecilion is a bet on the long term. Each skill launched adds a permanent charge which increases its damage and its maximum mana - a Cecilion which has farmed quietly for fifteen minutes no longer has anything to do with the one at the beginning.

On the other hand, he is extremely fragile before stacking, and his skills have a wide but slow zone. Faced with a team that attacks him early and often, he never reaches his level. He is the typical hero where the result depends on the pace of the game more than the duel.

novaria.summary: Ranged harassment mage, whose ultimate enlarges the silhouette of targets to make his shots easier to place.
novaria.analysis:
Novaria is played from afar. Her skill 1 places a sphere that hurts and slows down around her before exploding; her skill 2 makes a sphere return to her, giving it speed and the ability to pass through walls, then throws it back towards a hero, with damage that increases with the distance traveled. His spheres reveal nearby enemies, and his ultimate enlarges the impact zone of the heroes hit while revealing their surroundings: this is what makes his long shots reliable.

She has no stuns or freezes, only slows. His measured win rate remains below average at all ranks, but increases with game length and rises above fifty percent after the eighteenth minute. The measurements place her clearly in difficulty against Natalia, then against Zilong, Aldous, Ling and Estes.

eudora.summary: Explosion Mage: Each skill electrifies the target and strengthens the next, up to an area stun.
eudora.analysis:
Eudora works in sequence. Each of his skills electrifies targets hit, and the next skill gains an effect against an electrified target: skill 1 creates a chain that accelerates him and can reduce his cooldown by half, skill 2 changes from a single-target stun to an area stun, and the ultimate triggers an additional explosion around each electrified target. The right order turns a skill rotation into elimination and group control.

Without electrification applied, his skills lose their additional effects: a first failed skill breaks the sequence. His measured win rate is higher in short games and drops back to average after eighteen minutes. Patch 2.1.88 places her among the reinforced heroes, without the wiki detailing the modification. The measures place her in difficulty against Atlas, Masha, Barats and Leomord.

zetian.summary: Mage whose ultimate damages and stuns all opposing heroes, wherever they are on the map.
zetian.analysis:
Zetian combines harassment and global presence. Her skill 1 launches a wave that launches another on each hit, up to three, and she can move and cast other skills during this time; his skill 2 installs a spirit that slows, reduces magic defense and can be redirected. His ultimate accelerates his entire team, injures and briefly stuns each enemy hero and reveals their position: it weighs on a fight even launched on the other side of the map. Her passive also protects her, at long intervals, by pushing back and stunning heroes who approach her.

Its measured performance is regular rather than spectacular: victory rate close to average, with no marked difference depending on the duration of the game, and ban rate down slightly over thirty days. His passive's lifesteal only charges when hitting heroes with his first two skills. The measurements place her in difficulty against Valentina, Floryn, Mathilda, Uranus and Gloo.

vexana.summary: Control mage that summons a fighting guardian, much more effective, according to measurements, in short games than in long ones.
vexana.analysis:
Vexana harasses from a distance and controls on impact. His skill 1 is a projectile that stops on the first hero hit, frightens him and pushes him away before exploding on his neighbors; his skill 2 hits an area after a short delay. His ultimate throws enemies into the air as a guardian arrives, who then fights alongside him for several seconds and hits large areas. Its passive curses targets hit, which explode on their allies if they die.

The measurements place it in the average for all ranks, but with a clear slope: high victory rate in short games, below fifty percent beyond the sixteenth minute. Its delayed skill 2 gives the target time to exit the area. She is in difficulty facing Alice, X.Borg, Marcel, Natalia and Benedetta.

nana.summary: Harassment mage that incapacitates a target by transforming it, and survives a fatal blow once.
nana.analysis:
Nana wears down her opponents from afar with a boomerang that hits back and forth. His skill 2 launches Molina on an area: the heroes affected are transformed for a short time, slowed down and weakened against magic damage; if she doesn't hit anyone, Molina stays on the ground and chases the first hero who approaches. The ultimate hits an area three times and stuns enemies hit multiple times in a row. Her passive grants her, once every two and a half minutes, an invulnerable transformation at the moment she should die.

Its measured numbers are low: below average victory rate at all ranks, even lower in Mythic Glory, with no real improvement in long games. While transforming her passive, she cannot cast any skills, and a fallen Molina chooses her target herself from among the approaching heroes. The counter gaps remain modest; the clearest place her in difficulty against Gloo, then against Akai and Hylos.

valir.summary: Control mage that repeatedly knocks back and stuns, and whose fireballs recharge with each hero hit.
valir.analysis:
Valir strings together controls more than he explodes his targets. Each skill that hits places a burn on the target; at three burns, the fire explodes and stuns it, at most once every seven seconds on the same target. His skill 1 lasts for two charges and recovers one as soon as it hits a hero, which allows him to recast it almost without pause as long as he aims correctly; his skill 2 repels enemies to the end of its jet of flames. The ultimate frees him from his negative effects, accelerates him and strengthens his two skills for a few seconds: increased range for the fireball, wall of flames which slows down for skill 2.

His measured figures are consistent: above average win rate at each rank, low bans. He is most effective in short games, and his advantage reduces as the game lengthens. In Mid lane, the same build clearly dominates the others. The measurements place him in difficulty against Rafaela, Helcurt, Kaja, Mathilda and Natalia, and at ease against Fredrinn, Alice, Balmond and Leomord.

granger.summary: Magazine Shooter: His damage comes from his skills, not his attack speed.
granger.analysis:
Granger is not built like a classic shooter. His skill 1 fires six bullets, the last of which is always critical, and his passive converts the recharge reduction into a physical attack, which makes attack speed almost useless on him: you buy attack damage and penetration.

This gives it a very early peak of power, exploitable in the jungle from the first object. His fragility remains that of a shooter, aggravated by the lack of control, apart from the brief slowdown of his ultimate: poorly positioned, he only has his skill 2 and the rolls of his ultimate to hope to escape.

beatrix.summary: Shooter with four weapons, each with its own ultimate: she changes role depending on the weapon carried.
beatrix.analysis:
Beatrix is ​​actually four heroes. She carries two weapons at a time among four, and each redefines its range, its rate and its ultimate: a very long range sniper rifle, an explosive shotgun, a rapid rate assault rifle, an area grenade launcher.

The level of play consists of choosing the correct pair before the game, then alternating in combat. This is what makes it both very strong in competition and very punishing in ranked play: a bad pair, or a bad change at the wrong time, and it no longer has any damage at all.

melissa.summary: Defensive Shooter: Her ultimate creates an area that melee enemies cannot pass through.
melissa.analysis:
Melissa solves the classic shooter problem — getting dunked — with a direct response. His ultimate gives him a shield and places a circle that repels present opponents and anyone who tries to enter, interrupting their movements, allowing him to continue shooting while an assassin exhausts himself trying to enter.

She remains a standard shooter compared to the rest: good power build-up, decent damage, no threat beyond her reach. Against a ranged team that ignores it and punches through the zone, the ultimate loses most of its value.

miya.summary: Pure basic attack shooter: she gains momentum as long as she hits, and her ultimate makes her disappear the moment you aim her.
miya.analysis:
Miya bases everything on basic attack. Its passive stacks attack speed with each shot that hits, skill 1 adds additional arrows that also damage nearby targets, and skill 2 immobilizes an area before slowing down what's around it. Her ultimate removes the negative effects, makes her invisible and brings her out of this state with her passive already at full charge: it is used as much to escape as to return to the exchange at full speed. Its measured win rate increases slightly with the length of the game.

It has no instantaneous movement. Once the ultimate is used, she only has skill 2 left to slow down an attacker, and her pace drops as soon as she stops hitting a target. The countermeasures place her in difficulty against Beatrix, Granger, Gatotkaca, Karina and Belerick, with a gap which is found from the Mythical rank to the Mythical Glory rank.

hanabi.summary: Rebounding damage shooter, which controls don't hit while she's carrying a shield.
hanabi.analysis:
Hanabi inflicts her damage in ricochet: each basic attack or skill that hits sends blades back to neighboring enemies, making her effective in group fights and on waves. Her skill 1 gives her a shield, and as long as a shield protects her, control effects have no effect on her; part of the damage it inflicts also recharges this shield. His ultimate immobilizes the first hero hit before exploding around him.

However, she has no instantaneous movement: if the shield falls, she becomes an easy target to reach again. His measured win rate is highest in short games and declines significantly as they get longer, falling below fifty percent after the eighteenth minute. At the Mythical Glory rank, the measurements place her in difficulty against Lolita, Joy, Beatrix, Wanwan and Ixia.

lesley.summary: Ranged crit shooter, whose measured win rate goes from very low to high depending on the length of the game.
lesley.analysis:
Lesley plays on range and critical strike. If she hasn't taken damage in a few seconds, her passive lengthens her next basic attack and gives her a high critical chance, and any physical penetration she buys turns into critical damage. Skill 1 camouflages her and strengthens her attack, skill 2 pushes enemies in front of her while making her retreat, and the ultimate locks on to an opposing hero to shoot him four bullets in a row.

The price of this profile can be seen in the measurements: its victory rate across all ranks is below average, with a very low point in games lasting less than fourteen minutes, and only exceeds fifty percent from the eighteenth minute. Her passive cuts off as soon as she is hit, and the ultimate's bullets can be intercepted by another enemy hero placed in front of the target. The measurements place her in difficulty against Sun, Gloo, Estes, Tigreal and Mathilda.

obsidia.summary: Shooter who accumulates bone shards with each shot, and whose ultimate attaches her to her target, preventing any escape through a movement skill.
obsidia.analysis:
Obsidia charges her passive by hitting: each attack or skill on an enemy fills energy that forms bone shards, up to twenty-five, and each of her basic attacks sends all the shards hitting the target. Her skill 1, a needle thrown from range, brings three times more energy than an attack and triggers the shards on the first hero hit; her skill 2 gives her a brief burst of speed. The ultimate briefly stuns the first hero hit, pulls her to them and tethers the two for three seconds: the target can no longer use movement skills, Obsidia gains a shield and temporary shards, and can attack while moving.

She is one of the most contested heroines of the moment: third ban rate and fourth selection rate of all heroes, with a ban that exceeds half of the games from Mythic Honor and which has increased further over the last thirty days. Her measured win rate is above average, higher in games under sixteen minutes than beyond eighteen. The measurements place her in difficulty against Baxia, Diggie, Estes, Miya and Bruno.

bruno.summary: Critical shooter who plays with a ball: his skills give him critical chance, and his ultimate bounces from enemy to enemy.
bruno.analysis:
Bruno gains critical chance each time a skill deals damage, stacking; in return, he has more physical attack but benefits less from attack speed. His skill 1 reinforces his next attack with a ball shot that slows, then the ball falls to the ground: recovering it gives a new attack and reduces the recharge of his skill 2. That skill is a slide that briefly stuns enemies in its path and gives him a ball back. The ultimate hits a hero, knocks them back to the edge of his range, stuns and slows them greatly, then bounces to other enemies, targeting the heroes first.

His measured figures are solid and consistent: win rate above average at each rank and whatever the duration of the game, better in Mythic Glory, for almost zero bans. His best measured partner is Harith. The measurements place him in difficulty against Lolita, clearly, then against Lesley, Aamon, Karina and Saber.

layla.summary: Range shooter whose damage increases with distance, widely played at the front ranks and less and less as you go up.
layla.analysis:
Layla shoots from afar and has an interest in staying there: her passive increases her damage with distance, up to a maximum at long range. Her skill 1 launches a bomb which, if it hits, extends the range of her basic attacks and her skill 2 for a few seconds and speeds her up. Her skill 2 marks the target; then hitting a marked target deals damage around it and stuns it very briefly. The ultimate permanently extends the range of her attacks and her skill 2, and when cast fires a powerful shot in a straight line.

Her measured pick rate is high at Epic and Legend ranks and drops with each rank up to Mythic Glory, where her win rate is also lowest. She is very weak in games of less than twelve minutes, then above average between the fourteenth and the twentieth. She doesn't jump or teleport. The measurements put her in difficulty against Atlas, Johnson, Sun, Khufra and Hylos.

estes.summary: The crudest heal in the game: its ultimate regenerates the entire team for several seconds.
estes.analysis:
Estes does nothing but heal, but he does it at a volume that no other support reaches. In a prolonged fight around an objective, his ultimate can negate an entire composition's worth of sustained damage.

This also makes him the most context-dependent hero in the entire game. Against a team that buys healing reduction, or has an initiation capable of removing him first, he becomes almost useless. It only provides area slowdown, little damage and no mobility: if it doesn't heal, it doesn't exist.

angela.summary: Support that attaches to an ally across the map to strengthen and protect them from a distance.
angela.analysis:
Angela plays a second part in parallel with hers. Her ultimate allows her to join any ally anywhere, giving them a shield, and casts her skills at no mana cost while attached — she literally becomes an extension of the chosen player.

Used well, it allows a wielder to dive with a security they never would alone, and it appears on the other side of the map to turn around a skirmish. Used incorrectly, it passes the game attached to the wrong player and does not influence anything.

Mathilda is the most versatile support in the game today. His skill 2 involves an ally in his movement, which makes it possible to bring a fighter into contact as well as to get a shooter out of a bad position. His ultimate locks a target and serves as a targeted initiation.

She also inflicts significant magic damage, which makes her playable as a secondary assassin when the game goes badly. Its difficulty lies in reading: each move involves two players at a time, and an error costs two deaths instead of one.

rafaela.summary: Healing and resurrection support, which brings back a fallen ally without waiting for their respawn timer to end.
rafaela.analysis:
Rafaela combines care, speed and control. His skill 2 heals nearby allies, especially the most injured, and gives them speed with a brief immunity to slowdowns; his skill 1 automatically hits the three closest enemies, revealing them and slowing them; his ultimate stuns on a line. Its passive, above all, allows you to resurrect a fallen ally, who reappears at the base: an opposing elimination therefore costs your team less.

Patch 2.1.88 significantly reduced the base recharge of resurrection, while increasing the part that depends on the ally's reappearance time, strengthened skill 1 and lowered the mana cost of its other skills. His measured win rate is now well above average, and his ban rate is increasing over the last thirty days. Its limit is initiation: a single control, to aim in a straight line. The measurements place her in difficulty against Ixia, Odette, Estes, Layla and Silvanna.

floryn.summary: Global Healing Support: Her ultimate heals the entire team, regardless of where they are on the map.
floryn.analysis:
Floryn heals from a distance and without needing to target her allies. His skill 1 targets an enemy, and healing fruits then bounce towards nearby allies; his skill 2 briefly stuns and reveals enemies hit; his ultimate heals the entire team twice, regardless of distance, and instantly boosts shields and regeneration. His lantern improves his statistics and can be shared with an ally, who then receives a bonus for each of his treatments.

Its measured performance depends strongly on the duration of the game: high victory rate in short games, under fifty percent after the eighteenth minute. carmilla.summary: Support tank that links enemies together: control or damage on one spreads to the others.
carmilla.analysis:
Carmilla lives in contact. Her passive makes her steal part of the defenses of the heroes she touches, her flowers revolve around her wounding, slowing down more and more and healing her, and her skill 2 accumulates speed before relaunching on a target to stun it, especially the longer the charge lasts. His ultimate curses an area: enemies who remain there are immobilized then linked, and as long as they remain close, a control suffered by one applies to the others, with part of the damage.

This mechanic makes its value very dependent on its allies: its best measured duos show gaps among the strongest recorded, with Diggie, Floryn, Mathilda and Chip. If enemies move away from each other, the bond breaks. She is among the reinforced heroes of patch 2.1.88, with no details published on the wiki. The measurements place her in difficulty against X.Borg, Valentina, Natalia and Lesley.

marcel.summary: Control support whose ultimate freezes everything in a large area, except him and the allies he has protected.
marcel.analysis:
Marcel plays with Clemar, his photographer soul. His passive automatically photographs nearby enemy heroes, freezes them for a moment, inflicts real damage on them and gives a shield of the same value to Marcel and a nearby ally; his basic attacks increase with his resistances, and his additional HP becomes hybrid resistance. His skill 2 accelerates him, more when he runs towards an enemy hero, then makes him jump leaving behind the area of ​​his skill 1, which greatly slows down the heroes then hits them after a short delay. The ultimate freezes all units in a large area for two seconds, including projectiles, and leaves only Marcel and the allies carrying his shield free.

His metrics are among the strongest in the game: second win rate of all heroes, and a ban that climbs with rank, rare in Epic, in more than two games out of three in Mythic Glory. He is especially formidable early on: his win rate is highest in the shortest games and then drops with each duration period. Patch 2.2.16 extended the cooldowns of his skills 1 and 2 and his ultimate. The measures place him in difficulty against Floryn, Angela, Lesley, Esmeralda and Cyclops; his best measured partner is Kalea.

tigreal.summary: Historical initiator tank, capable of bringing together an entire team in a single ultimate.
tigreal.analysis:
Tigreal does one thing, and he does it better than almost anyone: pick up multiple opponents at once. The classic combo is to rush in with skill 2, then immediately chain the ultimate before the targets disperse — canceling the animation with a Flicker spell remains the most profitable technique to learn on him.

Its limit is clear: apart from its ultimate, it brings almost nothing. A Tigreal who missed his initiation leaves his team with four for around ten seconds. He's a hero of timing, not continuous presence.

franco.summary: Initiation tank whose entire part fits in a grappling hook: it removes a player from the map.
franco.analysis:
Franco does not play the same game as the other tanks. He's not looking to absorb damage, he's looking to remove an opponent from combat before it begins. A successful grapple on the opposing shooter, followed by the ultimate, is a dead player and a free objective.

Its entire value therefore rests on the precision of a slow projectile skill, which vision entirely determines. Franco plays in the bushes, not in the lane. A Franco who misses three grapples in a row is dead weight; a Franco who touches them wins the game alone.

khufra.summary: The tank that punishes mobility: its skill 1 cancels enemy dashes and jumps.
khufra.analysis:
Khufra exists to cater to a specific category of heroes—those who are constantly on the move. Its skill 2 changes it into a ball which throws into the air any enemy trying to cross it by moving, which neutralizes Fanny, Ling, Wanwan or Benedetta in a way that no other tank allows.

Apart from this response role, he remains an excellent initiator: his skill 1 launches him at the first opposing hero, throwing the enemies around into the air, and his ultimate pushes back the opponents in front of him, stunning them if they hit a wall. Its weakness is its recharge: apart from skills, Khufra is slow and easy to bypass.

belerick.summary: Taunt tank that responds to each series of blows received: the more you hit it, the more it hurts.
belerick.analysis:
Belerick is built to be hit. His passive shoots the nearest enemy as he takes damage, and increases the HP he gains from his items and emblems. Its two controls are provocations: skill 1 slows down on a line then provokes, after a short delay, the enemies remaining on the line, and the ultimate provokes everything around it. His skill 2 accelerates him, greatly slows down his target and heals him, and each trigger of the passive shortens its recharge.

Its damage depends on the damage it receives: a team that ignores it takes away most of its response, and the provocation of skill 1 gives time to leave the line. His measured win rate is highest in short games and declines slowly thereafter. The measurements place him in difficulty against Lesley, Beatrix, Brody, Natalia and Marcel.

atlas.summary: Initiator tank which attracts several heroes at once and places them wherever he decides.
atlas.analysis:
Atlas engages in two stages. His ultimate throws chains that slow down hit heroes while he channels, then, revived, pulls them towards him and crushes them in the chosen location; only a deletion can interrupt it. His skill 2 makes him come out of his armor to move faster, immune to slowdowns, before the machine joins him by stunning around it. Each skill launched creates a zone of cold around itself which slows down, then freezes the enemies who remain there.

His numbers vary depending on the rank: his measured victory rate is higher in Mythic and Mythic Honor than in Mythic Glory, where he is however more banned. He is among the reinforced heroes of patch 2.1.88, with no details published on the wiki. His best duets measured are with supports – Mathilda, Floryn, Estes, Rafaela – and the measurements place him clearly in difficulty against Marcel, then against Wanwan, Alice, Valentina and Lancelot.

barats.summary: Tank jungler whose mount grows with each skill that hits, and who swallows an opponent only to spit them out against a wall.
barats.analysis:
Barats plays on accumulation. Each skill that hits makes Detona, his mount, grow bigger and gives him additional defenses; at maximum charge, its basic attacks become area tramples which maintain the effect. Skill 2 slows down and brings enemies back towards him, and the ultimate throws Detona on the first enemy hit: the target is swallowed, neutralized, then spat out, and explodes with a stun if it hits a hero or a wall. Barats is unresponsive to controls during the maneuver.

Its measured performance is concentrated at the start of the game: high victory rate in short games, then below fifty percent after the sixteenth minute. It is growing in popularity, with selection and ban rates increasing over the last thirty days. The measurements place him very clearly in difficulty facing X.Borg, then facing Gord, Alice, Yve and Uranus.

minotaur.summary: Roam tank who heals his team as much as he protects them, and whose ultimate makes him go into a rage to strengthen his skills.
minotaur.analysis:
Minotaur provides two things: control and healing. His skill 1 makes him jump over an area, briefly throwing enemies and reinforcing his following attacks; his skill 2 heals the most injured ally nearby as well as himself. The ultimate hits the ground three times, slows down then throws it into the air, making it insensitive to controls during the attack and causing it to go into a rage: for several seconds, its skills are reinforced and its healing affects all nearby allies.

He is rarely banned despite a victory rate measured above average at all ranks, a gap which slowly erodes in long games. He is among the reinforced heroes of patch 2.1.88, with no details published on the wiki. The measurements place him in difficulty against Beatrix, Ixia, Carmilla, Alice and Yve.

alice.summary: Tank mage who settles among enemies: as long as her skills hit, she burns everything around her and heals herself.
alice.analysis:
Alice fights up close despite dealing magic damage. Two skills that hit in quick succession activate her passive, an aura that damages nearby enemies at regular intervals, heals her and speeds her up, and which each skill that hits a hero prolongs. Her skill 1 launches a blast of blood that she can join by teleporting; her skill 2, with short recharge, hurts and slows heavily around her, and burns more when the aura is active. The ultimate makes her immune to crowd control and reduces the damage she takes while it charges, then she lands back to the area, immobilizing enemies.

Her measured figures are average, with a victory rate that improves a little in long games and a more frequent ban in Mythic than in Mythic Glory. In jungle, the most played build is clearly more played than all the others. The measurements place her in difficulty against Angela, Floryn, Karrie, Estes and Valir, and comfortable against Chip, Gloo, Tigreal, Barats and Atlas.
